transferee_verbatim: MEB Loan Trust VIII, a[n] CORPORATION organized under the laws of NEW YORK
anomaly_description: Recorded 2024-02-19, approximately nineteen months after origination and in the same month SRC-010 Doc. 34 at 3 n.4 records SLS writing to Plaintiffs about the default. The instrument recites the assignee as a New York CORPORATION while every other source treats MEB as a trust.
innocent_explanation: Assignments are routinely prepared and recorded only when needed, which in practice means at or near default; recording lag is normal and in most states does not affect validity between the parties. The entity-type recital is most likely a form-field error by the preparer. NEITHER is evidence of invalidity.
notes: THE INSTRUMENT WAS NOT READ - SRC-021 quotes it. Execution and notarization dates are unknown and are exactly what the instrument would show.

anomaly_description: As of 2026-03-24 the registry names FREED 2022-HE1 as investor, while the recorded assignment (2024-02-19) and the servicer's own 2026-01-16 letter name MEB Loan Trust VIII.
innocent_explanation: 'Investor' in a registry lookup and 'owner of this loan' in a servicer letter are not necessarily the same question: a trust may hold the loan while a different entity is recorded as investor, and registry fields are servicer-populated and frequently stale. The lookup itself was not seen.
notes: THE HIGHEST-VALUE OWNERSHIP FINDING, AND ITS VALUE IS NOT WHAT IT FIRST APPEARS. This is not a title defect. It is documentary evidence that the DEFENDANTS' OWN RECORDS disagree about who owns this loan - a records-reliability point available without any standing problem, because it does not challenge the assignment.

anomaly_description: SRC-010 Doc. 34 at 3 n.4 says 'on or about June 20, 2024'. SRC-021 P24 says on or about July 7, 2024. The ledger books 'New Loan' on 07/07/24.
innocent_explanation: The legal transfer date, the effective date and the boarding date are three different events and routinely differ by days or weeks. Doc. 34's date is itself hedged ('on or about') and appears in a background footnote. There is no real conflict here.
notes: Recorded and dismissed. Would become material only if a 12 U.S.C. 2605(b)-(c) transfer-notice timing claim is pursued, which requires the actual notices.

anomaly_description: SRC-010 Doc. 34 at 3 n.4 recites that Shellpoint retained McCalla in July 2025. The ledger shows foreclosure-cost disbursements payable to 'McCalla Raymer Pierce, LLC' beginning 08/12/2024, eleven months earlier, and to 'MCCALLA RAYMER LIEBERT PIERCE, LLP' from 07/25/2025.
innocent_explanation: The 2024 disbursements may relate to the earlier SLS-era foreclosure that was later abandoned, with a fresh 2025 retention for the second process. The two payee spellings may be one firm before and after a name change, or two related entities. Doc. 34's footnote is background recited from the parties' materials, not a finding.
notes: Supports the two-distinct-foreclosure-processes reading already recorded at CON-004. If there were two processes, the second required its own notices and the adequacy of the first cannot be assumed to carry over.
